status: declared by the pull request that closes #1133 before any calibrated score was computed; a development study, never a verdict. Nothing is published: no published declaration, record or registration changes, no day after 2025-12-31 is scored, no lockbox day is scored, and no record in docs/runs/ is edited. Any change to the candidate is Eleonora's decision. Amendments made after a number was computed would be listed in `amendments` and named as such; there are none.
avenue: #809 (a walk-forward recalibration that can widen the upper tail, not only narrow it), unparked by the ruling of 22 October 2026 on #1133
hypothesis: H5 (primary goal): the SOFR - IORB spread distribution in bp. Step 3, calibration of the predictive law. Development tier. Fix 3 of the three fixes ruled on 22 October 2026 (fix 1 is #1115, fix 2 is #966)
target: spread_bps at the scored day, in basis points, as a 23-quantile distribution at each lead h = 1..5 (scoring_protocol.GRID)

base.name: spread_mr_fhs_mad20_f0.5 (#941), the declared variant of #836 and the best of #941's six on grid CRPS
base.module: repo_model.spread_mr_fhs on repo_model.spread_mean_reversion (#686), unchanged, walked as scripts/fhs_scale_941.py walks it
base.calendar_arm: the calendar-aware arm of #1115 (PR #1125) is not on main, so it is not the base. The base reads no calendar column and every figure here is provisional under the calendar-first rule (docs/research/provisional-calendar-register.md); it closes no question in either direction. The recalibrations are functions of the base's laws and outcomes, so they can be re-run unchanged on #1115's arm once it is on main
base.no_other_base: no other model, and no variant of the base, is calibrated

calibration.principle: at a refit, from cells (a past decision day, a lead) whose target row is at or before the anchor of the refit's decision day, the last row public at the decision instant (protocol_benchmarks._anchor); no later row enters. A past cell is the base's own law for that day and the panel's spread_bps at its target row
calibration.window: the 504 decision days before the refit day (two years of business days, the base model's training window), restricted as above
calibration.units: the score of a cell at level p is (y - q_p) / w with w = max(q_95 - q_05, 1.0 bp), the cell's own 90% width of the base law, so a correction travels with the width of the day it is applied to
calibration.conformal_rank: the ceil(p * (n + 1))-th smallest score, clamped to 1..n (split conformal)
calibration.lead: each lead h = 1..5 is calibrated on its own cells
calibration.refit: every 21 decision days, from the first decision day on which every lead has at least 250 past cells; the correction is kept between refits and the state is read afresh from each day's own anchor. Decision days before that have no calibrated law and are not scored by any arm, so every arm and the base are compared on the same days

arms.pooled: (a) at each of the 23 levels, q_p + w * (the conformal quantile at level p of the normalised scores), over all cells of the lead, pooled over regimes. It can move a level up or down
arms.state: (b) the same, on the past cells whose anchor row has the same as-of floor flag state as the decision day's anchor row; the pooled correction of (a) while that state has fewer than 100 past cells at the lead, and while the flag is undefined at the anchor. The regime is the flag, never the hindsight regime label of evaluation_splits
arms.state_tail: (c) (b), except that levels at or above 0.90 (0.90, 0.95, 0.975, 0.99) take q_50 + lambda_p * (q_p - q_50), lambda_p the conformal quantile at level p of (y - q_50) / max(q_p - q_50, 0.25 bp) over the same cells as (b), floored at 0. lambda_p is not capped, so the upper tail can widen by more than the body (avenue #809)

calibration.no_others: three arms, no grid over their constants (504, 250, 100, 21, 1.0, 0.25 and the 0.90 cut are declared once here); no arm is added after a number is computed

state.flag: the floor-period flag of Lens B (#958) as the directive #966 specifies it: at row r, the median over rows r-59..r of 100 * (SOFR - the ON RRP offering rate in force that row), in bp, is at most 1 bp, with at least 40 rows in the window. Undefined (None) before 40 rows
state.rate_in_force: the offering rate of the latest `on_rrp` entry of metadata/policy_events.json whose effective date and announcement date are both at or before the row's date: announcement-dated and public by the row (docs/decisions/policy-point-in-time.md). The rate series is not ingested here (#643)
state.status_of_966: OPEN. #966 (PR #981) is not on main. This study carries a local replica of the flag as #966's body specifies it, in repo_model.walk_calibration.floor_flag, because the directive says (b) and (c) use that flag. When #966 merges, whether the flag's definition there is the one used here, and whether (b) and (c) are re-run on it, is Eleonora's question (numbered in the pull request). The replica is on from 2021-04-21 to 2023-12-08 (last flagged row) and from 2024-02-14 to 2024-07-08, which is the quoted span of #966's flag
state.as_of_guard: at every refit day, the flag at its anchor is required to equal a flag rebuilt from the panel cut at that row (check_flag_as_of raises LookAheadError otherwise); the flag at any other row reads rows at or before it by construction, which tests/test_walk_calibration.py checks on every row of a synthetic panel

references.uncalibrated_base: the base above, on the same days
references.benchmarks: B1 and B2 of scoring protocol v1 (repo_model.protocol_benchmarks), and B1' of #960 beside B1 (repo_model.b1_calendar): a reference row, not a benchmark of the protocol; B1 stays as ruled

scoring.scorer: repo_model.scoring_protocol (#655), the development tier: no verdict, no registration
scoring.days: decision days with a calibrated law, whose five targets (h = 1..5 business days on the panel's calendar) fall on or before 2025-12-31; no day after 2025-12-31 is read; the scored days pass lockbox.require_unlocked
scoring.outcomes: the panel's spread_bps at the target day
scoring.paired: each arm and the base against B1, B1', B2 and (for the arms) the base: skill = mean(d) / mean(S(benchmark)) with d = S(benchmark) - S(candidate), positive favours the candidate; scoring_protocol.paired_tests, the studentized stationary bootstrap (ruling 1), mean block 10 business days, 10,000 draws, seed 1133; two-sided 90% interval. A comparison the studentization cannot resolve is reported as undefined, with the means
measures: grid CRPS (23 levels), pooled and by lead
upper-tail twCRPS, weight 1{z > 0 bp}, pooled and by lead

the scaled score of #967 beside the raw one: each cell's grid CRPS over the trailing-year median of B2's grid CRPS for cells of the same pressure-day type of the target (252 positions, the last 6 left out, 20 cells of a type at least), the mean over the five leads per decision day; decision days with no such scale are left out of that row only

coverage of the 50%, 80%, 90% and 98% bands (q25-q75, q10-q90, q05-q95, q01-q99) with a 90% stationary-bootstrap percentile interval (2,000 resamples), pooled, by lead, by regime and by pressure-day type
the exceedance rates of q05 and q95 and of q01 and q99, by lead and regime
scoring.hit_rules: OPEN QUESTION, Eleonora's (#993; coverage_tests.hit_sequence takes the rule as a required argument): whole-bp outcomes tie with a quantile. Both rules are reported, side by side, and neither is chosen. Upper exceedance: y > q ('above') or y >= q ('at_or_above'). Lower exceedance: y < q or y <= q, the mirror. A band is missed when the outcome is outside it, so under 'above' the band is closed ([q_lo, q_hi]) and under 'at_or_above' it is open
scoring.tests: repo_model.coverage_tests: kupiec (unconditional coverage), christoffersen_independence and christoffersen_conditional_coverage (#993), on the by-lead sequences of consecutive decision days, pooled and within a regime (a regime is a run of consecutive days, so all three); within a pressure-day type the Kupiec test only. Reporting only: no p-value is a gate

splits.pooled: one number per decision day (protocol section 3); the coverage measures are read on the cells (decision day, lead)
splits.regime: SplitDeclaration.regime of the target day (metadata/evaluation_splits.json): 2018-19, 2020, 2021-23, 2024, 2025-26; 2021-23 is called out. The flag is the calibration's state; the regime labels are only the report's split
splits.pressure_day_type: SplitDeclaration.reporting_day_type of the target day: quarter_end, month_end, tax_date, ordinary
splits.min_days: a group of fewer than 20 days is listed and not tested

rules: An arm's gain over the uncalibrated base is read as present on a split when the 90% interval of its grid-CRPS skill over the base excludes zero on the positive side, and as a loss when it excludes zero on the negative side; otherwise undecided. A point estimate alone is not read.
A pooled figure is never read without the regime and pressure-day-type splits beside it; a gain pooled and a loss in 2018-19, 2021-23 or on quarter-end days is reported as mixed.

A calibration measure moving toward its nominal value (coverage toward the band's level, an exceedance rate toward 1 - level) is reported with its interval; a hit-sequence p-value is reported as a p-value and is no gate.
(b) and (c) are read against (a), and (c) against (b), as the contribution of the state and of the separate tail.
Nothing in this study is a verdict, and the page says so. Whether any arm joins a candidate is Eleonora's decision.

long_run: the base walk (89 refits) and the calibration are arithmetic on the panel and are expected to finish well inside two hours; if the scoring step exceeds about two hours the pull request says so and gives the paste for her Mac (.claude/skills/long-run)
